sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Stone County
sections.html:
Deeds for Stone County property are filed with the Recorder of Deeds at East Fourth Street in Galena, suite 108-A. The phone is 417-357-6362, and the counter is staffed weekdays from eight to four. The elected Recorder leads a team of deputy recorders.

The same desk handles federal and state liens, DD-214 discharge papers and marriage licenses. Marriage license applications need an appointment.

Paper records in the Galena office go back to 1851, the year the county was organized. Newer documents can be searched on the iCounty portal at stonemo.icounty.com, which carries records from January 1, 1993 to today.

Call the office for the exact total on your deed before you mail it. Missouri law builds the price from a statutory base plus state user fees, and the final number turns on page count and document type.

Fees changed this year. Under Senate Bill 938, a flat $2.00 increase applies statewide from August 28, 2026, to recorded documents, marriage licenses and surveys or plats. A price sheet printed before that date is $2 short.

Statutory recorder charges under RSMo 59.310
ServiceStatutory amount
Recording a deed, first page$5
Recording, each added page$3
Copy of a recorded instrumentCapped at $2, then $1 a page
Certificate and seal$1
Release covering several items$5 for every extra item
Subdivision plat, per sheet$25
Surcharge for a nonconforming document$25

These amounts leave out the state user fees under RSMo 59.319, which the 2026 bill also rewrote.

Page one needs a three inch blank band across the top for the Recorder's stamp, plus three-quarters of an inch of clear paper on the remaining edges. A deed that breaks the margin rule may be sent back with a written reason, or the office can take it and charge the $25 surcharge.

  • Use unbound sheets, white or light in color, printed on one side in dark ink.
  • Set type at eight points or larger, and type each signer's name under the signature.
  • Under that top band on page one, show the title, date, grantors and their marital status, grantees and the legal description.
  • Give a mailing address for one grantee.

A deed with no legal description or no grantee address may be refused. The statute protects the deed's validity and constructive notice even when that information is missing, but the office will still decline to file it. Check both items against your draft before the trip to Galena, and read the page-one order again: title, date, parties, then the legal description. Bring your fee in a form the office accepts, and call ahead to learn which payment types the counter takes.

sections.h2: How recording ties to your property tax
sections.html:
The Assessor draws parcel lines from the warranty deeds the Recorder sends over, so a deed that never gets recorded leaves the tax map behind. The Assessor is at 106 East Fifth Street in Galena, with the real estate staff at 417-357-6145. That office normally closes the assessment books around July 1, and taxing districts generally set rates by September 1.

The Collector works from the Historic Courthouse at 108 East Fourth Street, phone 417-357-6124. Payment is due by December 31, delinquency starts January 1, and a mailed check needs a December 31 postmark. Cards cost 2.4 percent with a $1.95 floor. There is a courthouse drop box at the north entrance, emptied daily. For 2026, statements went out on November 13 and online payment opened November 6.

Card numbers spoken over the phone are not accepted, so pay at the counter or call the payment line printed on the statement.

  • Recorder of Deeds: 417-357-6362
  • Assessor, real estate: 417-357-6145
  • Assessor, personal property: 417-357-6141
  • Collector of Revenue: 417-357-6124

Missouri has a senior property tax credit freeze, and in Stone County the Collector's office runs it through an SB190 Tax Freeze Lead. Applications are closed for this cycle.

A qualifying owner can call 417-357-6124 to learn when applications reopen and what paperwork to bring. The credit limits growth in the residential real estate tax on a primary residence. The bill stays in place, and vehicle tax is not covered.

If you plan to sell, ask the Collector what a mid-year sale does to an approved freeze before you sign a contract.

Stone County had an estimated 32,503 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.6 percent from 2020. Owner-occupants live in 83.3 percent of homes. The 2020 to 2024 survey put the median owned home at $249,000 and rent at $896.

Housing units number 21,225 against 13,530 households. Homes outside that household count are mostly places people do not live in year round, so a seller of a vacation or seasonal house should expect buyers shopping with that in mind. Taney County holds most of Branson, and Stone County sat inside the Branson micropolitan area until 2023. Accommodation and food services sales hit $109.9 million in 2022, which points to a visitor economy.

Galena is the county seat and Kimberling City is the largest city. Blue Eye R-V, Crane R-III, Galena R-II, Hurley R-I and Reeds Spring R-IV run the public schools, and Shell Knob 78 operates one elementary. The tax statement names your district, and buyers often ask about it first.

sections.h2: What the recording step looks like at closing
sections.html:
Your title company usually handles recording. Knowing the sequence still helps. After closing, the signed deed travels to Galena with the fee. Staff look at the margins, the legal description and the grantee address, stamp the page and add it to the index. The Assessor then gets the warranty deed and redraws the parcel on the tax map.

Ask the title company to tell you when the deed was recorded. Tax bills follow the record owner, so a slow filing can mail a statement to the wrong name. Selling for cash with no lender in the deal means fewer parties to coordinate, yet the deed faces the same checks as any other. Keep a copy of the recorded deed with your closing papers.

sections.h2: Avoid overpaying for a copy of a deed
sections.html:
Order copies from the Recorder directly. The office has warned residents about mailers from outside companies that offer a certified deed copy for $87 or more and then simply order it from the county. State law caps a Recorder's copy at $2 for page one and $1 for each added page, with $1 more for a certificate.

The Recorder's page also points to DeedWatch.com, a free email alert that fires when a document is recorded against names or addresses you list. It cannot stop fraud, and the Recorder calls it an early warning.

faqs.q: Where is the Stone County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 108-A East Fourth Street, Galena, MO 65656. The phone is 417-357-6362, and the office is staffed weekdays from eight to four.

faqs.q: Can I search Stone County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, from January 1, 1993 forward through the county's iCounty portal. Older records sit in the Galena office, which holds paper back to 1851.

faqs.q: Did Missouri recording fees go up in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. Senate Bill 938 added a flat $2.00 starting August 28, 2026, on recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats or surveys. Ask for the total on your page count.

faqs.q: What if my deed misses the margin rules?
faqs.a: The Recorder may return it with a reason or record it for an extra $25. Page one needs a three inch blank band at the top.

faqs.q: When are Stone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By December 31, with delinquency from January 1. The Collector's line is 417-357-6124.
